newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's Forbes' unit buys Kahawatte Plantation.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's Forbes' unit buys Kahawatte Plantation.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Forbes Ceylon Ltd said that one of its units, Forbes Plantation Ltd, had bought a 51 percent stake in Kahawatte Plantations, which was sold on the stock exchange by the government on Monday.
A senior company official said Forbes bought the stake at 30.25 rupees per share, after the stock was put on bid on the stock exchange at a minimum price of 30 rupees.
The Sri Lankan government is selling stakes in estate firms on the stock exchange as part of its privatisation programme.

It sold the controlling iterest in Malwatte Valley Plantations Ltd last week to Wayamba Plantations (Pte) Ltd, and plans to sell government holding in two other estates -- Elpitiya and Elkaduwa -- on Tuesday and Wednesday.
The shares of Elpitiya and Elkaduwa will be put on bid at 30 rupees per share. Those of Malwatte were introduced at 40 rupees and sold for 61.
Sri Lanka began restructuring its ailing plantations sector by privatising the management of 23 estate firms, which own some 600,000 hectares of tea, rubber and coconut.
Privatisation began in 1995 when it sold 51 percent or, 10.2 million shares, to a strategic investor, gave 10 percent to workers and the balance to the public.
The government, however, retains one "golder share", which empowers it to intervene in case of mismanagement.
